text: Neighborhood. My old neighborhood was three blocks from the beach.
Block. The bakery is two blocks from my building.
Crosswalk. Wait at the crosswalk, the cars here do not stop.
Doorman. Ask the doorman, he knows everything about this street.
Crowded. The metro is crowded until nine in the morning.
Traffic. There is a lot of traffic on this avenue.
Rush hour. At rush hour it takes forty minutes to go four blocks.
Within walking distance. The park is within walking distance, so I never take the car.
Send me a photo of your street. I want to see where you live now.
Hold on. There are some trees, there's a crosswalk, and that is basically it.
Is it noisy? It looks like a big avenue behind you.
At rush hour there is a lot of traffic. On Sunday there isn't much noise at all.
And your building? Mine has nothing, not even an elevator.
There's a doorman, Jorge. He has been here longer than the building, I think.
Okay, but what is actually near you? Anything good?
Two blocks away there's the place where you buy bread, the bakery. It opens at six.
Six in the morning? Nothing opens at six here. Are there parks?
There aren't much, sorry, there aren't many parks, but one is within walking distance.
That sounds better than you said at the start. Is it crowded on Saturdays?
Very. And I like it, which I did not expect. There is no beach, but there are a hundred other things.

When we moved, it was only four miles, but it felt like another country. On my old street there was a bakery on the corner, and there were a lot of children my own age, so I was never inside the house. On the new one there is nothing on the corner, and for the first month I thought there was nobody under forty on the whole road. But the park is within walking distance, the library is two blocks away, and there isn't much traffic, so my mother lets me go on my own. It took me about three months to stop hating it. And the funny thing is, the street did not change at all. I did.

Welcome to the neighborhood walk. The whole route is six blocks and it takes about forty minutes at an easy pace. Start at the square behind you. On this first street there are a lot of small shops and two cafes, and the building on the left with the green door is the oldest one here. Now, on the second street, please be careful. There is only one crosswalk, at the far end, so cross there and never in the middle of the block. After that the park is within walking distance, about three minutes. One last thing. Do not do this walk at rush hour, between six and eight, because the sidewalks are crowded and there is too much traffic noise to hear anything I say.
